tasks.prompt: Order the full conventional train from raw water intake to the distribution system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surface water plant using conventional treatment and chlorine disinfection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: lake intake through treated water leaving the plant.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris at the raw water intake
Rapid mix disperses coagulant through the raw water
Flocculation gently builds large settleable floc
Sedimentation settles floc by gravity in the clarifier
Granular media filtration polishes the settled water
Chlorine disinfection inactivates remaining microorganisms
Clearwell storage holds finished water before high lift pumping to distribution

tasks.explanation: The full conventional train screens, coagulates, flocculates, settles, filters, disinfects, and only then stores finished water in the clearwell for pumping to distribution.

tasks.prompt: Order the direct filtration train for a low turbidity source water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant on a consistently low turbidity reservoir source, approved for direct filtration.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screened raw water through disinfected finished water, with no sedimentation basin.

cards.label: Screening removes coarse debris from the raw water
Coagulant is added and dispersed in the rapid mix
Brief flocculation forms small pin floc
Water passes directly to the granular media filters
Filters remove the floc and fine particles
Chlorine disinfection follows filtration

tasks.explanation: Direct filtration omits sedimentation, so coagulation, brief flocculation, and filtration must carry the full particle removal load before disinfection.

tasks.prompt: Order the membrane filtration train from intake to finished water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant using low pressure ultrafiltration membranes after coagulation pretreatment.
tasks.configuration: Scope: river intake through membrane permeate disinfection and storage.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris
Coagulant is mixed into the raw water as pretreatment
Flocculation forms floc ahead of the membranes
Membrane modules separate solids from the permeate by size exclusion
Permeate receives chlorine disinfection for a distribution residual
Finished water flows to clearwell storage

tasks.explanation: Membranes physically separate particles from the permeate, but a chlorine residual is still added after membrane filtration because membranes provide no lasting disinfectant residual.

tasks.prompt: Order the slow sand filtration train from intake to finished water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small Ontario system using slow sand filtration on a clean source water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screened raw water through the slow sand beds and disinfection.

cards.label: Intake screening removes coarse debris
Pre filtration or roughing filtration reduces the load on the beds
Slow sand beds develop a biological schmutzdecke layer on the sand surface
Water percolates slowly through the sand and the biological layer
Filtered water receives chlorine disinfection
Finished water flows to storage

tasks.explanation: Slow sand filtration relies on the biological layer that forms on the bed surface, so the beds run slowly and continuously, and disinfection still follows filtration.

tasks.prompt: Order the groundwater iron and manganese removal train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional groundwater plant treating well water with dissolved iron and manganese.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well water through aeration, oxidation, and filtration to storage.

cards.label: Well pump delivers raw groundwater to the plant
Aeration adds oxygen and strips dissolved gases
Chemical oxidant is added and detention allows iron and manganese to oxidize
Oxidized iron and manganese form solid particles
Granular media filtration removes the oxidized particles
Chlorine disinfection and storage complete the treated water

tasks.explanation: Dissolved iron and manganese must first be oxidized into solid particles by aeration and chemical oxidation with detention time, and only then can filtration remove them.

tasks.prompt: Order the lime soda ash softening train from raw water to finished water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant softening a hard groundwater source with lime and soda ash.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw water through softening, recarbonation, filtration, and disinfection.

cards.label: Rapid mix disperses lime and soda ash through the raw water
Flocculation builds the calcium and magnesium precipitate floc
Sedimentation settles the softening sludge by gravity
Recarbonation adds carbon dioxide to stabilize the softened water and lower pH
Granular media filtration polishes the stabilized water
Chlorine disinfection completes the finished water

tasks.explanation: Lime and soda ash precipitate hardness as a settleable floc, the sludge settles out, and recarbonation must stabilize the high pH water before filtration and disinfection.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence for supplying a neighbouring system through an emergency interconnection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario municipality asked to supply a neighbour whose plant is down for repairs.
tasks.configuration: Scope: request for emergency supply received through the interconnection in controlled operation.

cards.label: Confirm the request, the approvals, and the volume and duration the home system can spare
Inspect the interconnection chamber, valves, meter, and backflow preventer
Flush the interconnection line until the water runs clear
Open the supply valve slowly and set the agreed flow rate
Monitor pressures on both systems and the supplied volume total
Record the supply in both systems logs and notify the authorities the agreement requires

tasks.explanation: An emergency interconnection protects the home system first by confirming spare capacity, proves the line and backflow protection, and then supplies at a controlled, metered rate with both systems logging the transfer.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical addition sequence at the rapid mix of a conventional plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant adjusting alkalinity and feeding alum plus a polymer aid on a low alkalinity source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw water entering the rapid mix through flocculation basin inlet.

cards.label: Measure raw water pH, alkalinity, and turbidity before dosing
Add alkalinity supplement first where raw alkalinity is too low for coagulation
Add the primary coagulant at the point of maximum turbulence
Allow rapid mix to disperse the coagulant before any aid is added
Add polymer coagulant aid downstream of the rapid mix
Carry the dosed water into gentle flocculation

tasks.explanation: Coagulation chemistry is set in order: confirm the raw water, correct low alkalinity, disperse the primary coagulant at maximum turbulence, then add the aid where it can build floc rather than be torn apart.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to place a flocculation basin into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional three stage tapered flocculation basin being returned to service after cleaning.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty flocculation basin through normal operation at design flow.

cards.label: Inspect paddles, drives, and baffles and confirm the basin is clean
Fill the basin slowly with settled raw water from upstream
Start the paddle drives at the lowest speed setting
Introduce coagulated water from the rapid mix
Set the tapered speeds, highest in the first stage and lowest in the last
Observe floc size at the basin outlet and adjust speed or dose

tasks.explanation: A flocculation basin is filled and started gently, with tapered mixing that is strongest where floc is forming and gentlest where finished floc must not be sheared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to place a sedimentation basin into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rectangular sedimentation basin returned to service after a cleaning outage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clean empty clarifier through steady settled water flow to the filters.

cards.label: Inspect the basin, sludge collectors, and effluent weirs and confirm they are clean and level
Fill the basin slowly to avoid disturbing the inlet baffles
Start the sludge collection mechanism before flow is introduced
Introduce flocculated water at a reduced flow rate
Raise flow gradually to the normal rate once a sludge blanket forms
Check settled water turbidity at the effluent weir before sending full flow to the filters

tasks.explanation: A clarifier is filled slowly, its sludge collector runs before solids arrive, and flow is raised gradually so the sludge blanket and settled water quality are established before full production.

tasks.prompt: Order the full backwash sequence for a gravity granular media filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rapid gravity filter at the end of a run, washed with air scour and filtered water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter taken out of service through the end of the wash cycle.

cards.label: Close the filter influent valve and let the water level draw down
Close the filter effluent valve to isolate the filter from the clearwell
Open the waste drain valve to the backwash waste line
Start air scour to loosen the media bed
Start the backwash pump and raise wash water flow gradually
Wash until the waste water runs clear, then stop the pump and close the drain

tasks.explanation: Backwashing isolates the filter first, opens the waste path before any wash water flows, uses air scour to loosen deposits, and ends only when the waste water runs clear.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to return a freshly backwashed filter to service using filter to waste.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional rapid gravity filter that has just been backwashed and must ripen before production.
tasks.configuration: Scope: end of backwash through the filter going into full production.

cards.label: Allow the media bed to settle and the water above it to clear after backwashing
Open the influent valve and start filtration at a reduced rate to the waste line
Run filter to waste while effluent turbidity falls during ripening
Confirm filtered water turbidity meets the plant target on a grab sample or analyzer
Close the waste valve and open the effluent valve to the clearwell
Raise the filtration rate gradually to the normal production rate

tasks.explanation: A backwashed filter ripens as the bed re-forms its removal layer, so the first filtered water goes to waste until turbidity meets the target, and only then is the filter put into production.

tasks.prompt: Order the planned shutdown of a gravity filter for an extended outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter being removed from service for a week of underdrain repairs.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter in production through a drained and secured filter cell.

cards.label: Reduce plant flow or shift production to the remaining filters
Close the filter influent valve to stop flow into the cell
Close the filter effluent valve to isolate the cell from the clearwell
Open the drain and lower the water level to just above the media
Drain the remaining water slowly so the media bed is not disturbed
Lock out and tag the filter valves and record the shutdown in the log

tasks.explanation: A planned filter shutdown first protects plant production, then isolates the cell on both sides, drains it slowly to protect the media, and finishes with lockout and a log entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the jar test procedure used to select a coagulant dose.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench jar test on the day raw water, using six jars and a range of alum doses.
tasks.configuration: Scope: collecting the raw water sample through choosing the dose for the plant.

cards.label: Collect a fresh raw water sample and measure its turbidity, pH, and alkalinity
Fill each jar with the same measured volume of raw water
Add a different coagulant dose to each jar while rapid mixing
Rapid mix briefly to disperse the coagulant evenly
Slow mix to simulate flocculation and let floc form
Stop mixing and allow a set settling period
Measure the settled water turbidity in each jar and select the lowest dose that meets the target

tasks.explanation: A jar test mirrors the plant in miniature: identical raw water in every jar, a dose range added during rapid mix, then flocculation, settling, and a turbidity comparison to pick the dose.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence an operator follows to confirm chlorine CT compliance for the day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant disinfecting with free chlorine through a baffled clearwell under Ontario Regulation 170/03 practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the operating data through recording the CT result.

cards.label: Record the lowest clearwell water level and the corresponding contact volume
Determine the peak flow rate through the contactor for the period
Calculate the theoretical detention time from volume divided by peak flow
Apply the baffling factor to get the effective contact time T
Measure the free chlorine residual C at the contactor outlet and the water temperature and pH
Multiply C by T and compare the CT against the required value for the target inactivation

tasks.explanation: CT is concentration multiplied by effective contact time, so the operator must first fix the volume at its lowest level, use peak flow, correct detention time with the baffling factor, and only then multiply by the measured residual.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily clearwell operating sequence from plant start up to steady supply.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant with a two cell clearwell supplying high lift pumps.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clearwell level management through a normal production day.

cards.label: Confirm the clearwell level is above the minimum needed for disinfection credit
Start filtration at a rate matched to the expected demand
Verify the chlorine residual leaving the clearwell meets the target
Start high lift pumping to match distribution demand
Cycle clearwell level between the low and high set points through the day
Record levels, residuals, and volumes in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Clearwell operation protects disinfection credit first by holding the minimum level, then balances filtration inflow against high lift outflow while residuals and levels are logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the operating sequence used to turn over water in an elevated storage tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario distribution system with one elevated tank showing an aging chlorine residual.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a full draw down and refill cycle for water age control.

cards.label: Check the tank level trend and the chlorine residual at the tank sample point
Plan the draw down for a low demand period so system pressure is protected
Draw the tank down to its low operating level through normal demand
Refill the tank with freshly treated water at a controlled rate
Confirm the residual in the refilled tank has recovered to target
Record the turnover volumes and residuals in the operating log

tasks.explanation: Turnover replaces aged water with fresh treated water, but the draw down is timed to low demand and the refill is verified by residual recovery so pressure and quality are both protected.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for flushing one distribution hydrant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional routine hydrant flushing on a residential street in an Ontario municipality.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the hydrant through returning it to service.

cards.label: Notify affected customers and set up traffic control at the hydrant
Inspect the hydrant and confirm the drain and caps are in good condition
Attach a diffuser or hose to direct discharge away from traffic and property
Open the hydrant slowly to avoid a pressure surge
Flush until the water runs clear and measure the chlorine residual
Close the hydrant slowly, replace the caps, and record flow, clarity, and residual

tasks.explanation: A hydrant is opened and closed slowly to avoid water hammer, discharge is controlled for safety, and flushing continues until clarity and residual confirm the local water quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps of a unidirectional flushing program for one zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario utility running a unidirectional flushing program on a looped distribution zone.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program planning through the final zone flush and records.

cards.label: Map the zone and plan the flush sequence from the clean water source outward
Notify customers in the zone and schedule the work for low demand hours
Close valves to isolate one pipe segment and force flow in a single direction
Open the designated hydrant and flush at a velocity high enough to scour the main
Move segment by segment outward until the whole zone is flushed
Reopen valves in the planned order, confirm residuals, and complete the program records

tasks.explanation: Unidirectional flushing works outward from the cleanest water, isolating one segment at a time so full scouring velocity passes through each main in a single direction.

tasks.prompt: Order the disinfection and commissioning of a new watermain under Ontario practice.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new subdivision watermain in Ontario, disinfected by the continuous feed chlorine method.
tasks.configuration: Scope: installed and pressure tested main through final clearance to place it in service.

cards.label: Flush the new main to remove debris and dirty water
Fill the main with chlorinated water to the target chlorine dose
Hold the chlorinated water in the main for the required contact period
Flush the main until the chlorine residual matches the distribution system
Collect bacteriological samples on two consecutive days and receive absent results
Connect the main to the live system and place it in service

tasks.explanation: A new main is cleaned, disinfected with a held chlorine dose, flushed back to system residual, and only connected after two consecutive days of absent bacteriological results.

tasks.prompt: Order the return to service sequence after a watermain break repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional winter watermain break on an Ontario residential street, repaired with a clamped section.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the repaired section isolated in an excavated trench through restored service.

cards.label: Isolate the broken section and confirm the excavation is safe to work in
Repair the main using disinfected fittings and clean pipe handling
Flush the repaired section through a hydrant or blow off until the water runs clear
Restore the chlorine residual in the section to match the system
Collect a bacteriological sample from the repaired section where required
Reopen valves slowly, check pressure, and confirm service is restored to customers

tasks.explanation: After a break repair, the section is flushed clear and the residual restored before valves are reopened slowly, so repaired and disinfected pipe is not put back on customers without verification.

tasks.prompt: Order the response and reporting sequence for an adverse water quality incident in Ontario.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario municipal system that receives an adverse bacteriological result under Ontario Regulation 170/03.
tasks.configuration: Scope: receipt of an adverse laboratory result through the required notifications and resampling.

cards.label: Receive and confirm the adverse result from the licensed laboratory
Notify the local medical officer of health and the ministry spill action centre as soon as possible
Notify the owner and the overall responsible operator
Issue any public notice or advisory directed by the medical officer of health
Take corrective action such as flushing and raising the disinfectant residual
Collect resamples and confirm the follow up results before standing down the response

tasks.explanation: Ontario practice puts notification of the medical officer of health and the ministry first alongside corrective action, and the incident is not closed until resampling confirms the water is back to standard.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting a distribution chlorine residual sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional routine free chlorine residual check at a designated Ontario distribution sample station.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the sample tap through recording the result.

cards.label: Select the designated sample tap and remove any aerator or hose
Flush the tap at a steady flow for several minutes to draw fresh main water
Rinse the sample cell with the sample water
Fill the cell and add the DPD reagent for free chlorine
Read the residual in the colorimeter within the method time limit
Record the result, location, date, and time in the sampling log

tasks.explanation: A residual sample must represent the main, not the plumbing, so the tap is flushed first, the cell is rinsed with sample, and the DPD reading is taken within the method time.

tasks.prompt: Order the bacteriological sampling and chain of custody sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional routine distribution bacteriological sample in Ontario, collected in a sterile bottle with sodium thiosulfate.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the sterile bottle through delivery to the licensed laboratory.

cards.label: Wash hands and confirm the sterile bottle seal is intact and within its expiry
Disinfect the sample tap and flush it to draw fresh main water
Reduce the flow and fill the bottle without touching the rim or rinsing out the preservative
Cap the bottle immediately and label it with location, date, and time
Complete the chain of custody form and place the sample in a cooler with ice packs
Deliver the sample to the licensed laboratory within the allowed holding time

tasks.explanation: Bacteriological sampling protects sterility at every step: the tap is disinfected, the bottle is never rinsed or touched at the rim, and the chilled sample reaches the lab inside its holding time with custody paperwork.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a grab turbidity measurement on filtered water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench turbidimeter check of filter effluent at a small Ontario plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drawing the sample through recording the verified result.

cards.label: Draw the sample from the filter effluent tap after a brief flush
Fill a clean sample vial and wipe the outside dry and free of fingerprints
Insert the vial into the calibrated turbidimeter with the index mark aligned
Read and record the turbidity in NTU
Compare the result with the continuous analyzer reading
Investigate and note any difference beyond the plant tolerance

tasks.explanation: A grab turbidity result is only trustworthy with a clean, bubble free vial in a calibrated meter, and comparing it with the continuous analyzer verifies the online instrument.

tasks.prompt: Order the general lead sampling sequence at an Ontario school or day nursery plumbing system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario school sampled for lead in drinking water under Ontario Regulation 243/07 at a general level.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning the sampling visit through submission of the flushed and standing samples.

cards.label: Identify the drinking water fixtures to be sampled and prepare labelled bottles
Confirm the water has stood in the plumbing for the required standing period
Collect the standing sample from the fixture before any flushing
Flush the plumbing for the required period after the standing sample
Collect the flushed sample from the same fixture
Submit both samples with completed forms to the licensed laboratory

tasks.explanation: Lead sampling compares a standing sample, which captures lead leached during stagnation, with a flushed sample from the same fixture, so the standing sample must be taken before any water is run.

tasks.prompt: Order the receiving and storage checks for a bulk chemical delivery.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional delivery of bulk sodium hypochlorite to an Ontario treatment plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: tanker arriving at the plant gate through the chemical placed in storage.

cards.label: Verify the delivery paperwork matches the product and quantity ordered
Inspect the tanker connections and the plant fill line before transfer
Confirm the receiving tank has enough free volume for the delivery
Connect the transfer line and open valves in the correct order with spill containment in place
Monitor the transfer and tank level until the delivery is complete
Disconnect, close and tag the fill line, and record the delivery in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: A safe chemical transfer starts with paperwork, connections, and confirmed tank capacity, keeps containment in place during transfer, and ends with the fill point secured and the delivery logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a liquid alum feed system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional alum metering pump system being started at the beginning of a production run.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alum storage tank through a verified feed rate at the rapid mix.

cards.label: Confirm the alum tank level and that the suction line is flooded
Open the suction and discharge valves on the feed line
Prime the metering pump until alum flows without air
Start the pump at the calculated stroke and speed setting for the target dose
Confirm flow with a calibration column drawdown check
Verify the dose by jar test or settled water turbidity and trim the setting

tasks.explanation: A metering pump is primed on a flooded suction with valves lined up first, then set to the calculated dose and proven by a calibration drawdown before the dose is trusted.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a sodium hypochlorite feed system for disinfection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional 12 percent sodium hypochlorite feed system starting with the plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day tank check through a confirmed residual at the clearwell outlet.

cards.label: Check the hypochlorite day tank level and the age and strength of the solution
Open the suction and discharge valves and prime the metering pump
Start the feed pump paced to plant flow at the calculated dose
Confirm feed by a calibration column drawdown
Measure the free chlorine residual after the contact point
Adjust the dose so the clearwell outlet residual meets the target

tasks.explanation: Hypochlorite feed is proven at the pump by drawdown and proven in the water by the measured residual, with the dose trimmed only after both checks are known.

tasks.prompt: Order the overview sequence for starting a fluoride feed system where fluoridation is practised.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario plant that fluoridates, feeding a fluoride compound to finished water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: saturator or solution tank check through a verified fluoride residual in finished water.

cards.label: Confirm the fluoride solution tank level and that the feed line is intact
Line up the suction and discharge valves and prime the metering pump
Start the pump at the calculated setting for the target finished water concentration
Confirm the feed rate with a calibration drawdown
Collect a finished water sample and measure the fluoride concentration
Adjust the feed and record the dose and result in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Fluoride is fed to a tight target concentration, so the pump is set by calculation, proven by drawdown, and confirmed by a measured finished water concentration before adjustment.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a centrifugal treated water pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional high lift centrifugal pump being placed into service after a weekend shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump at rest through the pump running at its duty point.

cards.label: Inspect the pump and motor and confirm the area is clear and dry
Confirm the pump casing is primed and the suction valve is fully open
Check that the discharge valve is closed or at its start position
Start the motor and watch pressure and current as the pump comes up to speed
Open the discharge valve slowly until the duty flow is reached
Record flow, pressures, and any unusual noise or vibration

tasks.explanation: A centrifugal pump starts primed with suction open and discharge throttled, then the discharge is opened slowly to the duty point while pressures and current confirm a healthy start.

tasks.prompt: Order the planned shutdown of a centrifugal treated water pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional planned shutdown of one high lift pump for seal inspection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump running at duty through the pump secured at rest.

cards.label: Confirm another pump or storage can carry the demand while this pump is out
Close the discharge valve slowly to unload the pump
Stop the motor once flow has fallen to near zero
Close the suction valve to isolate the pump
Drain or vent the casing if the pump will be opened
Apply lockout and tagout and record the shutdown in the log

tasks.explanation: A planned shutdown unloads the pump by throttling the discharge before stopping the motor, then isolates, drains, and locks out the machine in that order.

tasks.prompt: Order the return of a disinfected well to service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional municipal well disinfected after pump replacement, under Ontario practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well disinfected and held through clearance sampling and connection to the system.

cards.label: Pump the well to waste until the heavy chlorine from disinfection is flushed out
Continue pumping until the chlorine residual falls to near the normal system level
Collect a bacteriological sample from the well sample tap
Receive an absent bacteriological result from the licensed laboratory
Place the well into service at a controlled rate
Monitor residual and turbidity as the well comes fully online

tasks.explanation: A disinfected well is pumped to waste until the strong chlorine is gone, and it is only connected after an absent bacteriological result confirms the disinfection worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the shock chlorination of a well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional shock chlorination of a drilled well after a positive routine sample investigation pointed to the well.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the chlorine solution through the disinfected well standing idle.

cards.label: Calculate the well water volume and the chlorine needed for the target shock dose
Mix the chlorine solution and confirm the well pump and controls are ready
Introduce the solution into the well so it reaches the full water column
Surge or circulate the water so chlorinated water contacts the casing and screen
Run each connected outlet until a strong chlorine odour or residual is detected, then close it
Let the chlorinated water stand in the well for the required contact period

tasks.explanation: Shock chlorination doses the whole well volume, works the solution through the casing and into every outlet, and then relies on standing contact time before the well is flushed and resampled.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleaning of a raw water intake screen.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional shoreline intake with a bar screen showing a rising differential level.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning the work through the screen returned to normal duty.

cards.label: Review the differential level trend and confirm the screen is fouling
Reduce plant flow or switch to the standby intake path if available
Isolate the screen bay and apply the required safety controls
Rake or wash the accumulated debris from the screen bars
Inspect the bars and guides for damage while the screen is clean
Return the bay to service and confirm the differential level has recovered

tasks.explanation: Screen cleaning is driven by the differential level, done with the bay isolated at reduced flow, and proven complete when the differential returns to normal.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleaning of a sedimentation basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional annual cleaning of a rectangular clarifier with accumulated sludge and algae.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin in service through the cleaned basin ready to refill.

cards.label: Shift production to the remaining basins and confirm plant capacity
Close the influent and effluent valves to isolate the basin
Drain the basin to the residuals handling system
Wash down walls, weirs, and baffles and remove the remaining sludge
Inspect the sludge collector, weirs, and coating while the basin is empty
Close the drain and record the basin as ready for a controlled refill

tasks.explanation: Basin cleaning isolates and drains the cell to residuals handling, washes and inspects it while empty, and leaves it ready for the slow controlled refill used at start up.

tasks.prompt: Order a filter media inspection during a drained filter outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional inspection of a dual media filter suspected of mudball formation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter drained for inspection through the inspection findings recorded.

cards.label: Drain the water to just below the media surface
Take core samples of media at several points across the bed
Measure the media depth and compare it with the design depth
Check the cores for mudballs, fouling, and media loss or mixing
Inspect the exposed underdrain and support gravel where visible
Record depths and findings and set the corrective work before refilling

tasks.explanation: A media inspection samples the bed itself: cores reveal mudballs and fouling, depth checks reveal media loss, and findings are recorded before the filter is returned to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting sequence when a filter backwash is not cleaning the bed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter whose post wash headloss stays high and whose waste water never ran dirty.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a completed wash that left the bed dirty through the confirmed root cause check.

cards.label: Review the backwash flow rate record against the design wash rate
Confirm the backwash pump delivered full flow for the full wash duration
Check that the air scour ran for its full set time before the water wash
Inspect the drained bed surface for mudballs and cracking
Check the wash water troughs and waste valve for partial blockage or leakage
Correct the cause found and repeat a supervised wash to confirm cleaning

tasks.explanation: Poor washing is traced in the order the wash happens: rate, duration, air scour, bed condition, and the waste path, then proven fixed by a supervised repeat wash.

tasks.prompt: Order the calibration check sequence for a continuous free chlorine analyzer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional online amperometric chlorine analyzer at the clearwell outlet.
tasks.configuration: Scope: taking the analyzer reading through returning it to service verified.

cards.label: Record the analyzer reading and the sample flow status
Collect a grab sample at the analyzer sample tap at the same moment
Measure the grab sample free chlorine on the bench DPD colorimeter
Compare the analyzer and bench results against the plant tolerance
Adjust or calibrate the analyzer if the difference is outside tolerance
Return the analyzer to service and record both readings in the log

tasks.explanation: An online analyzer is verified against a simultaneous grab sample measured by the reference bench method, and it is only adjusted when the paired readings fall outside tolerance.
